technical_change: SailPoint CLI 2.5.0 (PR #252, branch feature/DEVREL-3362) ships an updated OAuth authentication flow for the CLI. The official release notes do not elaborate on the specific mechanism changed (grant type, token storage, redirect handling, etc.) - the commit history only labels it 'new oauth flow'.
who_is_affected: Teams that script SailPoint ISC/IdentityIQ automation through the CLI and authenticate it via OAuth.
implementation_impact: Unconfirmed pending release-note detail. Recommend testing the 2.5.0 upgrade against existing CLI-driven pipelines in a non-production tenant before adopting, since OAuth flow changes can silently break scripted auth. Prior CLI releases in the same window (2.4.0 Aug 26, 2.3.0 Aug 20 migrating to golang-sdk v3) show active, fast-moving CLI development this cycle.
material_change_since_last: New finding - no prior scan on record for this console.

technical_change: CVE-2026-12342 (GHSA-m924-m654-f267): unauthenticated remote code execution on the IdentityIQ server, caused by improper input validation (CWE-20) of content submitted to the web service API. CVSS v3.1 base score 9.6 (Critical). GitHub Advisory Database / NVD describe it as impacting all versions of IdentityIQ; no fixed version is listed on the advisory itself. GHSA status: Unreviewed.
who_is_affected: On-premises IdentityIQ customers whose IdentityIQ web service API is network-reachable.
implementation_impact: Third-party security-news aggregators (not independently verified by this run — see notes) report SailPoint has released a fix identified as IIQSR-983 for supported IdentityIQ versions. sailpoint.com/security-advisories and community.sailpoint.com, which would carry the authoritative vendor advisory and patch instructions, were unreachable this run (DNS/egress blocked in this sandbox) and could not be opened to confirm patch details first-hand.

technical_change: CVE-2026-12341 (GHSA-7mfg-3gc5-q3w2): unauthenticated attacker can gain access to protected APIs and data due to improper validation of OAuth bearer tokens (CWE-287). CVSS v3.1 base score 8.8 (High). Described as impacting all versions of IdentityIQ; no fixed version listed on the advisory. GHSA status: Unreviewed.
who_is_affected: On-premises IdentityIQ customers exposing IdentityIQ APIs that rely on OAuth bearer token auth.
implementation_impact: Same caveat as the companion CVE-2026-12342 finding: SailPoint's own advisory page could not be opened this run (egress blocked), so patch/remediation detail is unconfirmed first-hand.

technical_change: Added a status_for_unique_account field to the saviynt_endpoint_resource Terraform resource, controlling which account statuses are checked for uniqueness in account-name rules (accepts numeric codes, text values, or comma-separated combinations; updatable in place without replacement).
who_is_affected: Customers managing Saviynt EIC endpoint resources as Terraform/IaC
implementation_impact: Minor schema addition to an existing resource; no breaking change noted in the release notes
material_change_since_last: First observation — console/data/findings.json did not previously exist for this skill instance. Not a verdict-changing finding: it is single-vendor, implementation-level evidence about Saviynt's Terraform provider only. No SailPoint or RSA equivalent evidence was gathered this run, so row E3 (SDK/CLI/Terraform/IaC support) remains unseeded per the absence rule — see skill/references/evidence-rules.md.

technical_change: Both the official TypeScript and Python SDKs added a script to generate an OAuth scopes file and added generic API endpoint support, as mirrored PRs in the same week. Remaining releases in the window (TS v2.2.48/50/51, Python v2.1.76/78/79) carried no described changes beyond a changelog diff link.
who_is_affected: Developers automating SailPoint ISC through the official SDKs
implementation_impact: Minor developer-experience / tooling change, not a new product capability. Continues to evidence an actively maintained public SDK ecosystem, which was already noted qualitatively in matrix row E3.
material_change_since_last: First observation logged for this item; too low-materiality on its own to move the E3 verdict out of unseeded.

technical_change: SailPoint CLI 2.8.0 adds a new `scope` command, makes OAuth scopes optional (PowerShell scopes are now read from a file instead of being hardcoded), updates connector subcommands to use the latest available API, and adds agent-skills setup for managed and unmanaged UI plugins. CLI terminology shifts from "ISC" toward "Identity Security" / "SHF" when describing a tenant.
who_is_affected: Customers and partners automating SailPoint Identity Security Cloud via the public CLI/SDKs.
implementation_impact: Low — additive CLI tooling change; the release page states no breaking change or deprecation.
